identity.title: BigCodeBench: Benchmarking Code Generation with Diverse Function Calls and Complex Instructions

problem.claim: Assess whether LLMs can solve challenging, practical programming tasks requiring multiple tool/function calls and compositional understanding of complex instructions.

gap.claim: Existing benchmarks mostly evaluate short, self-contained algorithmic tasks or standalone function calls, leaving broader multi-tool, instruction-heavy capability less assessed.

contributions.claim: Introduces BigCodeBench: 1,140 fine-grained tasks using multiple function calls from 139 libraries across 7 domains.
Defines tasks with an average of 5.6 test cases and 99% branch coverage, and proposes BigCodeBench-Instruct, which converts docstrings into concise essential-information instructions.
Reports evaluation results across 60 LLMs showing difficulty with precise function calling under complex instructions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their benchmark through diverse multi-library function calls, broad domain coverage, fine-grained tasks, and a natural-language-oriented instruction variant.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that evaluated LLM scores reach at most 60%, compared with reported human performance of 97%.
The authors report that LLMs are not yet capable of precisely following complex instructions while using function calls.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs increasingly automate tasks through Python code, spanning software engineering and general reasoning.
Prior benchmarks largely focus on short algorithmic tasks or standalone calls, while practical tasks require diverse tools and compositional reasoning over complex instructions.
The paper introduces BigCodeBench and its high-coverage task design, plus the BigCodeBench-Instruct variant.
Evaluation of 60 LLMs is reported to show a substantial gap from human performance, motivating further advances.

source_observation.claim: The benchmark explicitly aligns task construction with practical requirements—multiple tool calls and complex instructions—and reports both test-case counts and branch coverage.

lessons.interpretation: A capability claim is more informative when the evaluation structure directly represents the capability and exposes its testing coverage.
lessons.application: When proposing a benchmark, map each target capability to concrete task requirements and report coverage-oriented diagnostics alongside aggregate scores.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the research question concerns a narrowly defined primitive or when coverage metrics do not represent real-world use.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify how human performance was measured or whether the 60% and 97% figures are directly comparable.
Per-model scores, task-level error patterns, and details of the 139 libraries and 7 domains are not provided.
The abstract does not establish independent validity, reproducibility, or priority of the benchmark.
